title: Saving documents in Draft Mode
text:
Saving documents in Draft Mode 
 N avigation in Farvision 
 Saving documents in draft mode 
 Draft mode allows users to temporarily save typed data without storing the data in the actual transactional database. Large transactions can be saved in interim state as Draft mode for future use. User can resume re-entry of transactions from draft mode. 
 Transactions within draft mode are not available for any further subsequent processing. Draft Mode has to be set as ‘ON’ in the interface for Draft mode saving button to be enabled. There is no such setting required for Draft mode enabling. It is enabled by code only. 
 ‘Save As Draft’ is enabled under submit menu. 
 After a document is saved as draft, user can only retrieve it again after making draft mode on in the same interface. 
 Click on the row to open the screen and make further entry or necessary changes. After that user is required to finally submit and save the entry. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Queue Management for Reports
text:
Queue Management for Reports 
 Some common features of Farvision 
 Queue Management for Reports 
 Queue management allows for processing of data in the background so that the user does not have to wait while data is being processed. Once the report or process is completed a notification will be provided that the job has been completed. It is important to use queues so that server utilization is not disturbed during peak working hours. 
 There are two types of queues 
 Queue Reports 
 Queue Processes 
 Notifications 
 Desktop notification will be shown after completion of job. Report can be downloaded from the notification alert. Queue Reports 
Some reports and bulk print format can be queued. There are two types of processes 
 ● Fire and forget - the queue is started on demand when the report has to be processed 
 ● Repeat every few minutes - any data which is added for the bulk processing will be processed, and checking for new data will be done on a predefined frequency. 
 Fire and forget 
 A job id is assigned against reports which are being queued under fire and forget. A notification will be sent to the user’s device once the report is ready. Reports which have been queued can only be printed from the Queue management console. Queued reports cannot be printed (either PDF or Excel) from the menu interface from which generation of report was started. 
 Example : Application detail register, Booking register, Invoice register and Receipt register, Indent register, Purchase order register, Goods receipt Note register and Purchase Bill register. Examples for Bulk Printing of documents are Invoice, Booking annexure, Applicant Ledger. 
 Repeat every few minutes 
Queues which repeat every few minutes are used for bulk printing of documents. No job id assigned as it is a continuous loop where more documents which are added for bulk processes are picked up. After receiving the notification, search Bulk Printing in the menu column and then for the relevant menu Item. 
 Download : Once the report is complete, it can be downloaded and saved locally. The report will be automatically deleted after downloading. Reports will be visible in the queue console until the reports are downloaded. Users are allowed to download their reports while admin users can download report of any user. 
 Delete : Pending and generated report can be deleted. If the status is pending, the delete button will stop the processing of the report. If the status is Complete, delete will physically remove the report and it will not be available, it is deleted from the server. 
 Status : Pending, In Process, Complete, Error, No record found are the status of the queued report. 
 Remarks : This column provides details of the status. Example, For In process, it will show start. 
 Desktop notification will be shown after completion of the job. Hide Downloaded : On select of the Hide Downloaded check box, all downloaded row items will be hidden and only those row items will be shown which are pending for download. Queue Process 
 Some reports a process has to be run before the report can be generated. 
 Example : Finance module cash flow report generated through process method and process report will be downloaded from queue console under the Process tab. 
 Property management invoice generated through bulk invoice menu after notification will be downloaded from the queue console. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Data Import Process
text:
Data Import Process 
 Some common features of Farvision 
 Data Import Process 
 Data import allows data to be imported from excel sheets instead of entering through the interface. Data has to be entered in pre-defined excel sheets, checked for correctness and is then imported into Farvision. Data import is available for many masters and a few transactions, the process of importing is the same. Only the excel template is different in which data has to be entered. 
 Data import is normally used by first time users of Farvision, or if there is a huge volume. Bulk data can be inserted into Farvision and it saves time. Once your backlog is cleared, it is recommended to use the interface for day to day entry. Sometimes data import is also used where the number of rows in a document is very large, example a journal voucher with 200 lines. 
 There are four steps to be followed 
 ● Download Template 
 ● Upload Template 
 ● Validate Data 
 ● Import Data 
 DOWNLOAD TEMPLATE 
 Object: This is the master or transaction form for which the excel template has to be downloaded. 
 Nested Objects: Some forms which have to be imported have a lot of data, and have multiple excel worksheets in one excel template. These multiple worksheets normally correspond to tabs of the entry interface. Example, Account Head Import will have the worksheets for Ledger, Ledger Address, Ledger Communication, Ledger Contact, Bank Details, etc. 
 All these worksheets are linked to each other through a common field called Link Ref Code . The same value of this field in each row has to be entered under ImportLinkRefCode in the nested worksheets. In the Ledger worksheet Link Ref Code ‘1’ has details of Amar Singh, Link Ref Code ‘2’ has details of Amit Kumar Pal. In the Ledger Address worksheet, ImportLinkRefCode ‘1’ will contain address details of Amar Singh, Link Ref Code ‘2’ will contain address details of Amit Kumar Pal. The value given to the Link Ref Code and ImportLinkRefCode has to be the same so that data in the different worksheets can be associated with each other. 
 Download template : Download the template by clicking the Download button. An excel file will be downloaded on your local computer. Open the excel sheet. Enter the data in the excel sheet. 
 About the Excel Template 
 There may be one or more worksheets in which data has to or can be entered. Click on the different worksheets to enter data in them. Remember to use the same identifying value in all worksheets so that data between the different worksheets can be linked to each other. In case there is no data to be filled in the nested worksheets, leave it blank. Do not fill only the ImportLinkRefCode if no other data is available for entry in that sheet. In case there is a row in the main sheet but there is no associated data for that row in the linked sheets, skip that row number in the linked sheet. 
 Each excel template has an Info worksheet which will guide the user about the properties of the fields. 
 Sheet Name : Worksheet names are listed here. 
 Column Names : Fields available in all associated worksheets are listed here. Data has to be entered as rows, fields are the columns. 
 Properties : Fields can have the following properties 
 Is required: True - this is a mandatory field, has to be entered. 
 Is required: False - this is an optional field. 
 Max length: The maximum number of characters which can be entered in that field. 
 The following points have to be kept in mind while filling data in the prescribed excel sheet 
 Do not remove any columns or worksheets , even if there is no data to be entered in them. Format must be as per the original excel template downloaded. 
 Do not change any names, settings, alignment, formatting of fields, worksheet, or files . 
 Remove any hyperlinks from the data fields . Example Email. 
 Try to import records into batches of 100, 200 or 500 rows at a time. Import can be run multiple times. Data will keep on getting added in Farvision. 
 Fill all mandatory fields 
 Enter data in ImportLinkRefCode if data is there in the associated worksheets 
 Do not enter blank rows , especially at the end of the excel sheet 
 Wherever applicable, Debit and Credit amounts should tally . 
 Spelling of account heads, parent account, items, etc should be correct, i.e. match with the masters in Farvision 
 Wherever applicable, data in related sheets should tally with the data in the main sheet . Example, Receipt/Payment or Journals, the Adjustment Info amount for each party should tally with the amount in Ledger details for the same party. 
 Some tips 
 Clear cache and clear history of the browser, in case of unknown error 
 UPLOAD TEMPLATE 
 Upload the filled out excel Template to start the data uploading process. 
 Select File : Select the file in which data has been entered and has to be uploaded. 
 The template can be dragged and dropped or the same can be selected from its location. Click on the Drop files to upload panel. Select the file in which data has been entered and has to be uploaded. Click on the Upload button. Once the template has been uploaded, it will show the message Uploaded Successfully. Click on Next button to go to the data validation step. VALIDATE DATA Once the filled up excel has been uploaded, the data has to be validated from the template and click on Next 
 Process Queue : Click on the box so that the validation process can be routed through the Queue Management console. If the data volume is large, it is important to queue this process else the server will become very slow. 
 Validate Data : Click on the Start Validation button to start the validation process. 
 Status : While the data validation is ongoing, a status bar will show Validating Data, Please Wait. If the data validation is successful, it will show the status as Success. If data is not correct and has failed the validation process, it will show Error Found. 
 Result : In case the status is not successful, the reasons why validation has failed will be provided in this Excel file which can be downloaded. The file will have both data which has a problem and data which is correct. The data where there is a problem is highlighted in yellow. The problems with the data will be displayed in the Import Remarks column. In this example, HSN Id does not exist for Construction service in HSN Master. 
 In this example, Relationship should have Son or Wife, and the name Rakesh Kumar and Mahaveer Singh should have been entered in Relative Name respectively. 
 In this example, Postal code is a mandatory field that can’t be blank. 
 The validation routine has to be run repeatedly till there are no errors left. 
 Click on the Next button to go to the Import Data tab. 
 IMPORT DATA 
 Click on Start Import to start importing data from filled up excel template file into Farvision. On successful import, it will show the status as Success. Click on the Finish button. Data which has been imported can be checked in the respective Advanced Search for the transaction or master forms. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

text:
Resource_Requirement_Planning_Methodology

 Base

 Requirement 
 Analysis

 Against BOQ (coefficient based)

 Steps 
 to Follow 
 1. 
 For Lumpsum based quantity capping on procurement 
 2. 
 For Coefficient based quantity capping BOQ (coefficient based) 
 Requirement 
 Analysis 
 1 . Against 
 Activity 
 If customer has an only standard [like DSR] activity 
 master and he/she wants to define bill of material [means co-efficient] 
 against the activity master, this method can be used. 
 It can be used in Auto Indent, 
 Auto Issue and for that it needs to auto populate resource in BOQ AND 
 in Work Order and price list MUST be created before population 
 of the data. Price List can be created project wise. The entire data like 
 Budget, BOQ and Work Order must have minimum quantity variation at 
 enterprise level . Otherwise changes in drawing and design in a project 
 is difficult to manage in this method. [ Note - To do auto issue, 
 resource population in work order is always mandatory]. 
 Note - Indent amendment 
 cannot be done once the auto indent generated, whereas customer can completely 
 delete the indent and re generate. As well as any quantity changes can 
 be done before generation of the auto indent. This is a general note for 
 auto indent process 
 2 . Against 
 Activity with variant 
 Not 
 In Use [It was created to incorporate internal data]. Not for external 
 use. 
 3. 
 Against Project Budget 
 If customer wants to define Lump sum procurement 
 quantity control of item [Material] for sub project wise and Budget head 
 wise, this method can be used. In this method variance at any level can 
 be managed smoothly. 
 Auto indent can also be done but auto Issue cannot 
 be implemented. User can tag budget head at the time of doing issue entry 
 but the data will not reflect in Material Requirement & Utilization 
 Register (Against Budget) report. 
 Note - Indent 
 amendment cannot be done once the auto indent generated, whereas customer 
 can completely delete the indent and re generate. As well as any quantity 
 changes can be done before generation of the auto indent. This is a general 
 note for auto indent process 
 4. Against 
 BOQ (coefficient based) 
 If customer 
 wants to define BOQ and BOM against all the activities of BOQ. 
 Against 
 BOQ ( coefficient based ) 
 System automatically calculates 
 resource quantity based on the defined coefficient resource requirement 
 Need to have 
 detailed planning before execution. Lump sum procurement is not 
 possible 
 Real time tracking 
 of Material requirement and utilisation 
 Indenting cannot 
 be done without BOQ 
 Any change in BOQ 
 will automatically reflect on material requirement 
 Quantity in 
 BOQ cannot be reduced once indenting is done 
 Auto consumption 
 can also be used 
 Problems may 
 be faced if any activity has payment terms. Like MEP activity, 
 now there are four payment terms, like a. 20% advance b. 50% on 
 Supply c. 20% installation and d. 10% on testing. Hence 
 the auto consumption will follow the % mentioned above. It may 
 create the difference between actual consumption and booked consumption 
 Here auto 
 indent can be amended and customer needs to select Activity wise in Create 
 Indent Option in auto indent. 
 5. Against 
 BOQ (coefficient based) without Auto Indent 
 If customer 
 wants to define BOQ and BOM against all the activities of BOQ. 
 BOQ 
 coefficient based (Without Auto indent) 
 User can define coefficient 
 against BOQ and system will calculate material consumption based 
 on Work Done quantity as per coefficient 
 Detailed BOQ 
 will be required. Cannot be managed in lump sum contracts. 
 Any change in BOQ 
 will automatically reflect on material requirement 
 Auto Indent 
 MUST not be done. Hence no quantity capping is done at the time 
 of indent. 
 Auto Issue can also 
 be used 
 Procurement 
 will not be BOQ based. So, indenting will not lock the BOQ and 
 necessary changes can be done in BOQ at any given time. 
 Budgeting control 
 can still be managed through normal indent 
 Indent Quantity, 
 PO Quantity and Received Quantity will not be available in Material 
 Required vs utilisation Report. 
 Procurement will 
 not be BOQ based. So, indenting will not lock the BOQ and necessary 
 changes can be done in BOQ at any given time. 
 Procurement 
 will not be BOQ based. So, indenting will not lock the BOQ. Indenting 
 can be done more than required quantity. 
 Linked with BOQ activities 
 at the time of auto issue 
 Resource Requirement 
 is not required at the time of purchase and can be entered anytime

 What is a Drawing? 
 C lients can store 
 any architectural drawings or documents provided by an architect for a

 view and top view, and record the architect’s name in the engineering 
 module. 
 Drawing Group 
 Navigate to Engineering > Setup > 
 Drawing Management > Drawing Group 
 Purpose: 
 To categorise and store drawings related 
 to construction within specific groups, facilitating organized management, 
 and easy retrieval of drawings in the Engineering module. 
 Steps: 
 · Access the Engineering Module 
 Navigate 
 to Farvision UI Framework. 
 Select 
 the 'Engineering’ from the main menu. 
 Go 
 to 'Setup'. 
 Click 
 on 'Drawing Management'. 
 Select 
 'Drawing Group'. 
 · Enter Main Information 
 Code: Enter 
 the unique code for the drawing group (e.g., GROUP A). 
 Description: Provide a description for the drawing group (e.g., 
 GROUP A). 
 Option Type: Select the type of option, in this case, 'Drawing' 
 from the dropdown. 
 Submit the Information 
 Review the entered details. 
 Click on the 'Submit' button to create 
 and save the drawing group.

 Tutorial: 
 Creating Activity 
 Activity 
 Activity is basically the description 
 of the smallest executable unit of work. BOQ is the 1st place where activity 
 is mapped with its required quantity. Later on this Activity flows to 
 Resource requirement, Work order, WBS, DPR and finally in contractor RA 
 Bill. Activity is created through activity master and later on which can 
 be tagged in different transaction (s) 
 Use Case 
 Developers in a construction company 
 use the Activity functionality to efficiently manage and track 
 the smallest executable units of work. 
 The developer initiates this by entering 
 a detailed description of the smallest units of work, called activities, 
 into the system through the Activity Master. They then map these activities 
 with their required quantities in the BOQ. 
 Once the activities are defined and 
 mapped in the BOQ, the developer associates these activities with specific 
 resource requirements and work orders. This ensures that the necessary 
 resources and tasks are allocated to each activity. 
 The activities, once defined and associated 
 with the resource requirements, are then integrated into WBS to provide 
 a hierarchical representation of the project’s deliverables. Additionally, 
 the data from the activities flows into the DPR, providing real-time tracking 
 of progress against planned activities. 
 Finally, the mapped activities are utilised 
 for generating Contractor Running Account (RA) bills, providing a comprehensive 
 basis for billing and payment processes. 
 Throughout the entire process, the developer 
 can tag the defined activities in different transactions, allowing for 
 seamless integration and traceability across various project management 
 functions. 
 An Activity is used in BOQ, Resource Requirement, 
 Work Order and Work Order Amendment

title: Milestone
text:
Milestone 
 Help > Setup > Milestone Setup" />
 Tutorial: 
 Creating Milestone 
 Milestone 
 The 
 term ‘Milestone’ is used to designate a particular unit location of the 
 project. 
 For 
 example, in a real estate project, milestone usually refers to a particular 
 floor such as Ground floor, 1st floor, 2nd floor etc. 
 Use Case 
 A 
 construction company is overseeing the development of a high-rise residential 
 building. To effectively manage the progress and construction milestones 
 of the project, the company utilises the concept of Milestones to designate 
 specific unit locations within the building. 
 For 
 instance, within the context of the real estate project, the term ‘Milestone’ 
 is employed to designate and track the completion of each floor within 
 the building. The Ground Floor, 1st Floor, 2nd Floor, and subsequent levels 
 serve as distinct milestones, representing critical stages of the construction 
 process. Each milestone signifies the completion of a significant phase 
 of the project’s vertical development and is crucial for monitoring progress 
 and coordinating subsequent construction activities. 
 Business Unit : Select business unit. 
 (Select 
 the project under which Milestone is to be created) 
 Sub Project : Select 
 sub project. (It is basically tower or villa or row house or commercial 
 building under the project) 
 Code : Specify the milestone code. 
 (It 
 is basically a short name/nick name of a milestone) 
 Description : Enter the description 
 of the milestone 
 Milestone Group : Select 
 the milestone group which is already created in Milestone 
 Group master (means the immediate parent of the milestone.) 
 'Predecessor', 'Relation' and 'Lag 
 Day' are only to be used if user further wants to create a relation between 
 two milestones. 
 For 
 example : Predecessor of milestone '2nd floor' is '1st floor'. 
 'Predecessor', 
 'Relation' and 'Lag Day' fields will be enabled at the time of creating 
 second milestone i.e. successor. 
 Predecessor : It is the milestone 
 which will be executed before this 
 Relation : Enter the relation between 
 predecessor and the successor 
 Relation 
 can be of four types as shown below: 
 Start-Start : This relation denotes 
 job of two milestones (both predecessor and successor) will start 
 simultaneously 
 Finish-Finish : This relation denotes 
 job of two milestones (both predecessor and successor) will finish 
 simultaneously 
 Finish-Start : This relation denotes 
 job of one milestone (predecessor) will finish then the job of other 
 milestone (successor) will start 
 Start-Finish : This relation denotes 
 job of one milestone (predecessor) will start after finishing the 
 job of other milestone (successor) 
 Lag 
 time creates a delay between two milestone works that share a dependency 
 relation. For example, if user wants a 2 day delay between the end of 
 the first milestone and the start of the second one, create a Finish-Start 
 dependency between the two tasks, and then add 2 days of lag time 
 before the start of the second task. 
 Lag Day : Enter number of lag day(s). 
 If user wants to delay between the successor task (new milestone) and 
 predecessor task, then the number of days the task will be delayed to 
 start is called lag day. 
 Note: Lag Day will 
 be zero for 'Start-Start' and 'Finish-Finish' relations. 
 Tutorial: 
 Creating Milestone 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

 Tutorial: Creating Budget Head 
 Budget 
 Head 
 The Budget Head is a master setup 
 that is created for expenditure or income heads. To define the budget 
 head for expected inflow of cash in the business, select the inflow 
 option, and for expected expenses of money in the business, select the 
 outflow option. When creating a budget head, it should be assigned 
 to a specific Budget Group using the ‘Belongs To’ field. 
 Use Case 
 In a construction project management, 
 the Budget Head functionality is utilised effectively to manage 
 project finances. 
 The project finance team accesses the 
 Budget Head master setup to establish the necessary categories 
 for expenses and income related to the construction project. 
 To allocate funds for expected cash 
 inflows such as client payments or investments, the team selects the ‘inflow’ 
 option when creating the budget head. Conversely, for anticipated expenses 
 like materials, labour costs, or equipment purchases, the team opts for 
 the ‘outflow’ option. 
 During the creation of each Budget 
 Head, the team ensures that it is appropriately assigned to a specific 
 Budget Group using the ‘belongs to’ field. 
 The data associated with Budget Heads 
 is then integrated into reports, providing stakeholders with detailed 
 insights into the project’s financial performance. 
 Main Info

 and the code is unique

 The old Budget head has to discontinue and a new one made.

 you also need to tag the posting head for labour (labour cost will post

 For accounting 
 based budget head you need to tag the posting head where you want to post

title: Price List
text:
Price List 
 Help > Setup > Price List Setup" />
 Tutorial: Creating Price List 
 Price 
 List 
 Price 
 List is a listing of budgeted 
 rate 
 for labour, materials and equipment. A price list normally contains Srl 
 No, Resource Type, Name and Rate. 
 Use Case 
 In the real estate industry, a developer 
 could use a price list to create and manage expected budgets for various 
 construction projects. For instance, the construction company could utilise 
 a price list to estimate costs for various parameters required for the 
 project. 
 The price list would contain essential 
 details such as Serial Number, Resource Type, Name, and Rate for each 
 item. For example, under the ‘Resources Type’ category, various items 
 can be listed such as cement, steel, bricks, labour, heavy machinery, 
 etc. Each item would have a corresponding rate associated with it, reflecting 
 the cost of procurement. 
 In this model, the cost of materials 
 is user-defined. As specific materials are entered, they are automatically 
 computed during resource planning in: Engineering> Estimation> 
 Resource Requirement. 
 During resource planning, the price 
 list is retrieved from this section. The resource amount calculation is 
 then derived from the quantity and the user-defined price list. By using 
 the price list, the developers can monitor expected budgets for different 
 aspects of the construction process. 
 It is required to create a price 
 list at project level or even at work order level. 
 If price list is created at project 
 level, it means all the work orders will get the same expected rates (price) 
 for different resource types as labour, material and equipment under that 
 project. 
 If user creates price list at work 
 order level, then for each and every work order the rates of the different

title: Note For Approval
text:
Note For Approval 
 Help > General" />
 Note For Approval 
 The 
 Note for Approval is a structured document or form that outlines 
 specific parameters or requests requiring approval from the management. 
 This note typically includes details such as payment terms, final negotiations, 
 retention money, vendor scope, and other critical aspects of a business 
 transaction or decision. It serves as a formal communication tool to seek 
 authorisation or sign-off from relevant management personnel before proceeding 
 with any work order. 
 What Is the Benefit of Note for Approval? 
 One of the significant advantages of 
 creating a Note for Approval is that it helps ensure proper control 
 over key business decisions and processes. By explicitly documenting and 
 seeking approval for various parameters, organisations can enforce accountability, 
 prevent unauthorised actions, and reduce risks associated with unchecked 
 operations. 
 Use Case 
 Consider a scenario where a company 
 is finalising a contract with a new vendor for a major project. Before 
 officially committing to the agreement, the contractors’ team created 
 a Note for Approval detailing the negotiated payment terms, final 
 scope of work, vendor responsibilities, and retention money requirements. 
 This note is then routed to the management team, including the finance 
 and operations heads, for their review and approval. 
 Upon receiving the ‘note for approval’, 
 the management team can assess the terms outlined, ensure alignment with 
 the company’s goals and policies, and provide their approval or suggest 
 modifications if necessary. Once all stakeholders have reviewed and signed 
 off on the ‘note for approval’, the contractors’ team can proceed with 
 executing the contract, knowing that all critical aspects have been appropriately 
 vetted and approved. 
 Steps to Create Note for Approval 
 1. 
 Navigate to Engineering> General> Note for Approval. The 
 following window can be seen. 
 2. 
 Fill in the mandatory fields such 
 as Business Unit, Financial Year, Document Type, and Supplier . 
 For the other fields, fill the ones applicable for the project. After 
 filling in the necessary field, the following window can be seen. 
 Business Unit : Choose the applicable 
 Business Unit. 
 Financial Year : By default, current 
 financial year will be auto-populated otherwise it can be changed according 
 to the user requirement. 
 Document Type: The categorisation of a document based on its purpose 
 or function, such as purchase order or work order. 
 Document Date: The date when a specific document is created or issued. 
 Document No : A unique identifier 
 assigned to a specific document for tracking and reference purposes. This 
 is also auto-populated. 
 Supplier : The entity or organisation 
 from which the services are to be procured. 
 Original/Amendment : If the WO 
 is new, choose the Original option. If it is selected as Amendment, after 
 entering the Previous Contract Amount and the Amendment Value, it gets 
 tagged in WO Amendment under Amendment module. 
 Previous Contract Details : Information 
 about the previous agreement or contract, including relevant terms and 
 conditions. 
 Previous Contract Amount: 
 The monetary value associated with 
 the previous contract. 
 Proposed Order Value: The total amount proposed for the order 
 (applicable only if the work order is new). 
 Amendment Value : In case of amendment 
 work order, this value is applicable. 
 Subject : A brief description 
 or title of the document, summarizing its content. 
 Scope of Work : The tasks, activities, 
 and deliverables included in the project or contract. 
 Technical Specification : Detailed 
 descriptions of the technical requirements, standards, and features related 
 to the project or procurement. 
 Payment Terms : The agreed-upon 
 conditions and schedule for making payments on the contract or order. 
 Final Negotiation : The last stage 
 of discussions and agreements before finalizing the terms of the contract 
 or order. 
 Retention Money : A portion of 
 the payment was withheld to ensure the fulfillment of contractual obligations, 
 often released after the completion of the contract. 
 Billing Procedure : The method 
 and process for generating and submitting invoices for the goods or services 
 provided. 
 Our Scope: The specific areas 
 of responsibility or deliverables assigned to the organisation issuing 
 the document. 
 Vendor Scope : The specific areas 
 of responsibility or deliverables assigned to the vendor or supplier. 
 Mode of Measurement : The method 
 or criteria used to quantify or measure the work or services provided. 
 Workmen Compensation Policy : 
 The insurance policy providing coverage for work-related injuries or illnesses 
 suffered by employees. 
 PF No./ESIC : Provident Fund (PF) 
 Number and Employee State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) details, pertaining 
 to social security measures for employees. 
 Labour License : The official 
 authorisation or permit required for engaging in labour for specific activities. 
 CAR Policy/Third Party (Developers 
 Scope) : Contingent Auto Repair (CAR) Policy or insurance coverage 
 for damages to third-party property caused during project execution. 
 Warranty/Guarantee : The assurance 
 provided by the supplier regarding the quality and performance of goods 
 or services, often including specified warranty periods. 
 Safety Parameters : The defined 
 measures and standards for ensuring safety and minimizing risks during 
 project execution. 
 Drawing No.: The unique identifier 
 assigned to technical, or engineering drawings related to the project 
 or contract. 
 Remarks : Additional comments, 
 notes, or observations relevant to the document or its contents. 
 3. Click 
 on Submit once done. 
 4. Now, click on the Advanced Search Icon 
 on the top-right corner of the screen. From there the new entry made is 
 visible. 
 Now, navigate to Engineering> General> 
 Work Order. There is an option to tag this newly created Note for Approval 
 for that specific BU under the Creating Work Order tab . 
 This implies that after obtaining the Note for Approval, it can be mapped 
 against the Work Order. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: DPR Entry
text:
DPR Entry 
 Help > General" />
 Tutorial: 
 Creating DPR 
 DPR 
 Entry 
 DPR (Daily Progress Report) is 
 a written document describing the development of daily activities of a 
 project. 
 Benefits of Creating a DPR Entry for a Project 
 The utilisation of DPR enables stakeholders 
 to track and monitor the daily activities and progress of a project in 
 a systematic and organised manner. This documentation helps in improving 
 communication, providing transparency, identifying potential delays or 
 issues early on, and ensuring that the project stays on schedule and within 
 budget. 
 Use Case 
 Let’s 
 take an example where a developer working on the construction of a new 
 project, he can utilise Daily 
 Progress Reports to monitor the work completed each day, track any 
 challenges and obstacles encountered, document any deviations from the 
 original plan, and communicate updates to key stakeholders such as investors, 
 contractors, and regulatory authorities. By consistently generating and 
 sharing DPRs, the developer can ensure that the project is advancing as 
 per the schedule and address any issues promptly to prevent delays or 
 cost overruns.

title: Bank Guarantee
text:
Bank Guarantee 
 Help > Payment" />
 Bank Guarantee 
 Bank Guarantee interface 
 is used to 
 maintain the Work Order wise guarantee details with guarantee amount and 
 related expiry date. 
 Why is Bank Guarantee Interface Beneficial? 
 The Bank Guarantee interface 
 provides a centralised platform for accurately documenting and tracking 
 work order-wise guarantee details, ensuring transparency and reducing 
 the potential for errors and discrepancies. 
 By maintaining an up-to-date record 
 of guarantee amount and expiry dates, organisations can mitigate the risk 
 of unintentional oversights of expired guarantees, allowing greater financial 
 security. 
 By systematically storing and monitoring 
 guarantee information, this interface aids in risk mitigation by providing 
 the upcoming expirations and facilitating timely renewal or replacement 
 actions. 
 Use Case 
 With 
 the help of the Bank 
 Guarantee interface, a construction company efficiently manages guarantee 
 details for multiple ongoing projects. By inputting the guarantee amount 
 and expiry date for each WO, the company ensures that financial safeguards 
 are in place to cover any contractual obligations. In the event of a project 
 extension or modification, stakeholders can easily update the guarantee 
 information within the interface, maintaining accurate and current records.

title: Retention Release
text:
Retention Release 
 Help > Payment" />
 Tutorial: 
 Creating Retention Release 
 Retention 
 Release 
 Retention Release refers to the process of releasing retention funds 
 held by a client or developer as security against defects in construction 
 work or services provided. Retention funds are typically a percentage 
 of total contract value withheld by the client or developer until the 
 completion of the project to ensure that the contractor fulfills all obligations, 
 delivers quality work, and address any defects that may arise post-construction. 
 Benefits of Retention Release Interface 
 The release of retention funds acts 
 as a financial incentive for contractors to complete satisfactory work. 
 It ensures that the contractor rectifies 
 any defects or issues within a specified period before the release of 
 funds, thereby guaranteeing quality workmanship. 
 The retention release interface safeguards 
 clients from poor work quality and incentivize contractors to deliver 
 on their promises. 
 Use Case 
 After the final bill for a construction 
 project is passed, the system would release the corresponding retention 
 amount to the contractor at the appropriate time. The retention amount 
 and the designated time frame are already mentioned in the contract clauses. 
 The retention against order amount can be released through 
 this interface. This interface also shows retention amount released earlier.

 Info

 Select business unit 
 As soon as the business unit is selected, financial

 which has now been just released is displayed here 
 Narration : Any comments on retention 
 release can be entered here

 Info

 Bill Info, select the bill and click on the row. The following window 
 will open 
 Enter 
 retention release amount in 'Now Release' and save

 A new feature incorporated to release the Additional Security Deposit

 A new feature incorporated to release the Liquidity Damage (LID) amount

title: Payment Requisition
text:
Payment Requisition 
 Help > Payment" />
 Payment 
 Requisition 
 A payment requisition refers 
 to the formal request made by the Engineering, Material, or any other 
 department to their Accounts/Finance Team to make payment to their creditors 
 (supplier, contractor, or any payable account). 
 Benefits of Creating Payment Requisition 
 By documenting and formalising payment 
 requests, the system ensures that all payments are authorised and supported 
 by valid documentation, which helps prevent unauthorised or fraudulent 
 payments. 
 The payment requisition process provides 
 transparency by creating a clear trail of communication and approval for 
 each payment, enhancing accountability and reducing the risk of disputes. 
 Use Case 
 In 
 a real estate development project, a contractor completes a milestone 
 according to the agreed-upon work order. The contractor then submits a 
 payment 
 requisition, attaching relevant documentation such as invoices, time 
 sheets, or completion certificates. The Payment 
 Requisition is routed to the concerned team for review and approval. 
 Once approved, the request is forwarded to the finance department for 
 processing. The finance team verifies the documentation and processes 
 the payment according to the approved amount and schedule. 
 Steps to Create Payment Requisition 
 1. 1. Navigate to Engineering> 
 Payment> Payment Requisition. The following window can be seen. 
 1 . 2.Enter 
 the data into the respective fields: 
 Business Unit (Mandatory): 
 Choose the preferred Business Unit 
 Financial Year (Mandatory) : Auto-populated 
 Document Type (Mandatory) : This 
 is system generated. There are multiple options available in this field. 
 Choose the Payment Requisition (PREQ) option. 
 Document Date: Date on which the document is created. 
 Document No : This is the number 
 of the specific document after it has been created. 
 Adjustment Type : This option 
 is also system generated. The options available under this field are as 
 follows: 
 · On A/C: Adjustment 
 made on account. 
 · Advance : Payment made in advance before 
 the receipt of goods or services. 
 · Bill : Adjustment related to an invoice 
 or bill received from a supplier 
 General Ledger / Sub Ledger (Normal): Standard 
 adjustments recorded in the general or sub-ledger accounts. 
 Choose ‘On 
 A/c’ or ‘Bill’ option, 
 as applicable in this context. 
 Entry Type: This is the type of entry 
 against which the Payment Requisition is made. These are also system 
 generated. Choose Work Order from the list. 
 Search Account Head: Click on the Advanced Search Icon to 
 view all the entries and make the selection. The Account Head and 
 Parent Account head fields will be auto populated. 
 Account Head (Mandatory): Choose the 
 necessary account head. 
 Parent Account Head: Upon selecting 
 the Account Head, this field will be auto-populated 
 Narration: Add any remarks (if applicable). 
 2. 3. After the fields are filled, click on 
 the Add New Row option, upon which the following section will unlock. 
 The Parent Account Head is auto-populated 
 along with the Eligible Amount. 
 1. 4. 
 Insert the Amount 
 applicable and click on Next. 
 1 . 5. 
 Keep clicking on Next until 
 the Adjustment Info tab appears. Click on Add New Row upon 
 which the following window will appear. 
 1. 6.Choose 
 the Type and insert the Amount. Click on Save once 
 done. 
 1. 7. The following entry can be seen. Click 
 on Next. 
 1. 8. 
 The Statutory Info tab will open where the user-generated TDS and 
 GST amounts are shown. Click on Finish to complete the setup. 
 1 . 9 . The 
 following screen can be seen where the Sanction Amount and the 
 balance after deducting the sanction amount can be seen. Click on Submit 
 to save the entry. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Resource Requirement
text:
Resource Requirement 
 Help > Estimation" />
 Tutorial: 
 Creating Resource Requirement 
 Resource 
 Requirement 
 Resource Requirement refers to the specific needs for labour, 
 materials, equipment, and other resources necessary for the successful 
 completion of a real estate project. 
 Benefits of Assigning Resource Requirement for a 
 Project 
 The benefit of the resource requirement 
 interface allows effective planning and managing the allocation of resources, 
 ensuring that the right resources are available at the right time and 
 place. This facilitates efficient project execution, cost control, and 
 timely completion. 
 Use Case 
 When planning the construction of a 
 new complex, the resource requirement interface can be used to outline 
 construction materials and any other resources essential for the project. 
 By accurately forecasting and managing these requirements, the developers 
 can ensure that the construction progresses smoothly, stays within budget, 
 and meets the scheduled timeline. 
 Requirement 
 of resources during project life cycle are to be created. Resources can 
 be of three types namely labour, material and equipment. 
 Option 
 Type 
 Following 
 are different option types available based on which resources are required 
 A. 
 Option Type - Against Activity 
 Activity : 
 Search and select activity from the following window (Data comes from 
 Setup > Activity Setup > Activity ) 
 Add New Row: 
 After selecting activity, click '+Add New Row'. 'Add Resource' window 
 will open. 
 Purpose : 
 Select purpose 
 Resource 
 Type : Select resource type as Labour or Material or Activity. 
 1. 
 Resource Type - Labour : If 'Labour' is selected as resource 
 type, then resource name will be labour 
 2 . Resource Type - Material : If 'Material' 
 is selected as resource type, then a list of materials will appear 
 Select required 
 material from the drop down list 
 Unit : 
 Select unit of measurement 
 Quantity : 
 Enter material quantity 
 Rate : 
 Enter rate of the material 
 Amount : 
 Amount gets populated 
 Wastage(%) : 
 Enter percentage of wastage 
 Click 'Save' 
 to add resource. 
 3 . Resource Type - Equipment : If 'Equipment' 
 is selected as resource type, then a list of equipments will appear 
 B. 
 Option Type - Against 
 Milestone Enterprise wise 
 Milestone : 
 Select milestone name 
 Click 'Add 
 New Row', select 'Unit', enter seconds and rate. Amount gets populated. 
 Enter wastage(%). 
 Click 'Save'. 
 C . 
 Option Type - Against 
 Milestone Business Unit Wise 
 Business 
 Unit : Select business unit 
 Milestone : 
 Select milestone 
 Click 'Add 
 New Row', after entering required details click 'Save'. 
 D . 
 Option Type - Against 
 Project Budget 
 Business Unit : 
 Select business unit 
 Sub 
 Project : Select sub project 
 Document 
 No : Select document number 
 Budget 
 Head : Search and select budget head 
 Click 'Add New Row', after entering required details 
 click 'Save'. 
 E . 
 Option Type - Against 
 BOQ 
 F . 
 Option Type - Against 
 Work Order (Lumpsum) 
 G . 
 Option Type - Against 
 Work Order (Activity Wise) 
 Notes: 
 1. Against 
 the Project Budget option user can search the Resource details by using 
 the Resource Code. 
 2. A new 
 feature incorporated as now by using the Item code user can add the Resource 
 in the Resource Requirement against the different option types. 
 Currently 
 option provided after selecting the Resource Name, Resource Code will 
 be auto selected (Same as Item Master). 
 3. 
 A new feature incorporated in the Resource 
 Requirement and Option Type - Against Activity. As now by using Copy From 
 option user can create the Resource Requirement against an activity based 
 on the existing Activity Resource Requirement. This option is only applicable 
 in New/Create Mode, not in Edit mode. 
 4. During 
 Issue entry (From Material Module and Type of Document should be – Issue (Against 
 Milestone Sub Project Wise ) system will validate each Item wise total 
 Resource Requirement quantity against the Option Type - Against Milestone 
 Sub Project Wise. 
 Tutorial: 
 Creating Resource Requirement 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

Auto Issue 
 Help > Estimation" />
 Auto Issue 
 Auto 
 Issue interface helps to issue material against work done and on the basis 
 of own material or contractor material or loan material. 
 Main Info 
 As 
 soon as the business unit is selected, financial year, document type and

 Document 
 No : It is generated after saving the entry 
 Option 
 Type : Select option type 
 Work 
 Done No : Search and select the work done number 
 Basis : 
 Select the basis 
 Warehouse: 
 system will auto select the same Warehouse 
 against an item in the Item Info tab. This selection is optional and informative.

 There 
 are four options under 'Generate' as 'Main Activity With Original Items' 
 and 'Main Activity With Substitute Items', 'Sub Con Activity With Original

 Click on 
 the item row to open 'Detail Info' 
 Enter 'This 
 Issue Quantity' and select the warehouse.

title: Substitute Item
text:
Substitute Item 
 Help > Estimation" />
 Tutorial: 
 Creating Substitute Item 
 Substitute 
 Item 
 Substitution 
 of any item is required due to result of changed conditions. Sometimes 
 the base item may not be available at the market at the time of purchase 
 or sometime it might have turned costly. 
 Benefits of Substitute Item 
 The Substitute Item interface 
 allows for the customisation of substitute items based on specific project 
 requirements, such as material availability, cost considerations, and 
 quality standards. 
 Users can efficiently manage, and store 
 data related to substitute items, ensuring easy access and retrieval when 
 needed for various projects. 
 The interface enables seamless integration 
 of substitute item details with overall budgets, allowing for better cost 
 management and control. 
 The interface provides a structured 
 workflow for the approval of substitute items, ensuring that all stakeholders 
 are involved in the decision-making process. 
 Use Case 
 Consider a scenario where due to unforeseen 
 supply chain disruptions, the original construction material specified 
 for the flooring becomes unavailable. 
 The developer can now navigate to the 
 substitute item creation interface. They input the necessary details of 
 alternative flooring materials that meet the required specifications. 
 The system then integrates these substitute items with the project’s budget, 
 allowing the developer to assess the cost implications and make informed 
 decisions. 
 Material 
 Item : Search to select material item. Items 
 are displayed from the Item Master in Material Module. 
 Select item(s) 
 to be used as substitute for material item chosen. 
 Tutorial: 
 Creating Substitute Item 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Project Budget Amendment
text:
Project Budget Amendment 
 Help > Amendment" />
 Tutorial: 
 Creating Project Budget Amendment 
 Project 
 Budget Amendment 
 The Project Budget Amendment is the 
 act of revising or altering the original Project Budget. The “Project 
 Budget Amendment“ interface is used to keep track of all alterations carried 
 out for particular Project budget of the Business unit and Subproject. 
 Main Info 
 Business 
 Unit: Select the Concerned 
 Business Unit Name from Drop down. 
 As soon as the Business unit is selected, 
 Financial Year, Document type and Document date get populated. 
 Document 
 No: The Document number 
 will be generated automatically after saving the entry with suffix of 
 Revision Number.(For Example - PRBUD/00148/19-20/008) 
 Subproject: 
 Select the Concerned Subproject Name 
 from Drop down. 
 As soon as the Subproject is selected 
 Area, Unit, Project Length, Unit, Duration and remarks detail get auto 
 populated. 
 Revision 
 No: The revision no is 
 automatically generated as per the revision exist for the combination 
 selected. 
 Amendment 
 Reason: Reason for this amendment need to mention. 
 Out 
 Flow 
 Three parameters 
 A. Increase/Decrease in existing Budget 
 head 
 B. Add new Budget head 
 C. Remove Existing Budget head 
 A. Increase/Decrease 
 in existing Budget head 
 Step1 
 Step2 
 Step3 
 Increase the Budget Amount 
 Decrease the Budget Amount 
 Click 
 the Save Button and the Amount get updated against that budget head and 
 seen as mentioned below. 
 *In 
 case of multiple budget head user has to repeat above process multiple 
 time. 
 B. Add new 
 Budget head 
 Step1 
 Select 
 Budget group first and then select Budget Head belongs to that Budget 
 Group. 
 Step2 
 Step3 
 Once user clicks on save button 
 same row will get updated in Project Budget. 
 C . Remove 
 Existing Budget head 
 User 
 requires to click on checkbox of that Budget head which he/she wants to 
 remove, after that click on remove Row. 
 Notes: 
 1. 
 Once user removes the Budget head from Amendment screen but same will 
 available (Seen) in Project Budget Screen. 
 2. Once user removes the Budget Head 
 (Project Budget Amendment) the same budget head will not available for 
 addition in this project Budget Head. 
 3. 
 It’s advisable not to remove the budget head (Considering Above Two Mentioned 
 Point). Just decrease the amount and keep it as Zero, For Example: Budget 
 head - Civil Work – Rs. 10,000/ and its utilization against this Budget 
 Head is Rs. 5,000/-. Just decrease the Budget head by Rs. (-5,000/-) and 
 save the amendment. 
 4. while 
 doing amendment entry under Max Executed Amount column now Purchase Order 
 Amount also incorporated. Earlier only BOQ/Work Order Amount only were 
 coming on whichever is higher basis. Now BOQ/Work Order/Purchase Order 
 amount will appear and methodology will remain same as whichever is higher. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Work Order Amendment
text:
Work Order Amendment 
 Help > Amendment" />
 Tutorial: Creating 
 Work Order Amendment 
 Work Order 
 Amendment 
 The Work Order Amendment is the act of revising or altering 
 the original work order. The ‘Work Order Amendment’ interface is used 
 to keep track of all alterations carried out for a particular work order. 
 Main 
 Info 
 Business 
 Unit : Select the concerned Business Unit’s name 
 As soon as the business unit is selected, financial 
 year, document type and document date get populated 
 Document 
 No : The document number will be generated automatically after saving 
 the entry 
 Contractor 
 Name : Search or enter the name of the contractor 
 Parent Contractor : Parent contractor 
 is auto populated after choosing contractor name 
 Work 
 Order No : Search or enter the work order number (Data comes from General 
 > Work 
 Order ) 
 Amendment Type: Select amendment 
 type from the available options amendment, cancel and short close 
 Payment Term: Now 
 during Work Order Amendment user can mention the Payment term. This feature is only applicable 
 for those Work Order against which Payment term already mentioned in the 
 Work Order itself, else not. 
 Item Info 
 Under 
 'Item Info' click create From Work Order 
 'Tag 
 Work Order Amendment' window will open 
 Select 
 work order for amendment and click 'Save' 
 U nder Item 
 Info tab, Payment Term Group and Payment Term option added. 
 Activity 
 Detail Info 
 Select 
 'Edit' under 'Action' 
 Inc/Dec Quantity : Enter increase 
 or decrease quantity. (For example order quantity can be increased or 
 decreased) 
 Amended Rate : Rate can also be amended 
 as per requirement 
 Remaining 
 Quantity, Amended Quantity, Remaining Amount and Amended Amount will be 
 automatically updated accordingly. 
 Dimension 
 Click 
 'Finish'. The details row is now updated with the amendment details. 
 Billing 
 Term 
 Click 
 on GST row to open "GST Info" to update GST details 
 Click 
 on TDS row to open "Tax deducted at source" to update TDS details 
 Notes: 
 1. 
 A new validation 
 incorporated as while generating the Work Order Amendment, Completion 
 date cannot be less than from the Vendor Invoice Date of latest Contractor 
 RA Bill. 
 2. A 
 new feature incorporated in the web approval against the Work Order Amendment, 
 as during Work Order Amendment approval now we will get the Work Order 
 Amendment Activity details from the Activity info. 
 So if 
 approval authority wants to view the activity details while approving 
 the Work Order Amendment then it is needed to click on the Activity Info 
 option. 
 3. A 
 new feature incorporated in the web approval against the Work Order Amendment,

title: Daily Labour Entry
text:
Daily Labour Entry 
 Tutorial" />
 Daily Labour 
 Entry 
 Sometimes it is required to appoint Contractor to 
 supply daily labour to execute specific jobs. This document will guide 
 to record Daily Labour Activity through Work Done entry in Farvision. 
 1. Creating Type of Document 
 Path: Administration > Company 
 > Document Type 
 A new document type has to be 
 created where Entry Type will be WORK DONE and Category has to be selected 
 as DAILY LABOUR ENTRY 
 2. 
 Creating Work Order entry for Daily Labour activity 
 Path: Engineering > General 
 > Work 
 Order 
 Like the other Work Order, Daily 
 Labour activity related work order has to be prepared with the activity 
 mentioned for Daily Labour work. 
 3. Creating Work Done entry for 
 Daily Labour activity 
 Path: Engineering 
 > General > Work 
 Done 
 To do Work Done entry for Daily Labour user has 
 to open Work Done entry screen. After selecting the Business Unit, Document 
 type has to be selected as the document Type which is marked as DAILY 
 LABOUR ENTRY. 
 After selecting the Document Type, user has to 
 select Contractor Name and Work Order No against which Daily Labour entry 
 will be done. Now in Item Info tab, User has to select the required Activity 
 from the list of activities. 
 To put the details Work Certification, user has 
 to click on the actual Activity and has to put In Time, Out Time and then 
 in Certify Quantity, no of Labour worked has to be entered. 
 After putting the data, system will calculate total 
 hours of work and show full data on screen. 
 Now the entire Work Done for Daily Labour entry 
 can be saved by clicking the Submit button and then the work done is now 
 ready for Bill passing. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Price Variance and General Escalation
text:
Price Variance and General Escalation 
 Tutorial" />
 Price Variance 
 & General Escalation 
 Resource Requirement 
 Price Variance, General 
 Escalation & Coordination Process Budget Head Tagging 
 Work Order Wise Base Rate 
 General Escalation Parameter 
 Work Order Wise Co-Ordination 
 CFI Material Definition 
 Work Order Wise Approved Rate 
 Goods Receipt Note (GRN) 
 Contractor Material Consumption 
 (Auto Issue) 
 Price Variance 
 General Escalation 
 Co-Ordination Charges CFI 
 Co-Ordination Charges NSC 
 1. Resource Requirement 
 Estimation 
 > 
 Resource Requirement > Type against Work Order (Activity wise-lump 
 sum) If 
 contractor bought some materials for some specific activity and against 
 that items Price Variation will be calculated than this Resource type 
 will be required where ‘Executed By’ will be mentioned as Contractor 
 Supply. At the time of contractor material consumption entry, system 
 will calculate the Item consumption quantity from this Resource requirement 
 entry. 
 2. Price Variance, General Escalation 
 & Co-ordination Process Budget Head Tagging 
 Engineering 
 > Setup 
 > Budget Tagging for Price Variance & General Escalation 
 For each project, Budget Amount is determined against each expense. System 
 will check Price Variation and General Escalation expenses on the Budget 
 Amount defined against the same. To identify the respective Budget Heads 
 this screen will be used. 
 3. Work Order Wise Base Rate 
 Engineering 
 > Escalation > Work 
 Order wise Base Rate 
 At the time 
 of starting of the work, an agreement is prepared between Company and 
 Contractor that against a specific Work Order if the contractor bought 
 some Materials on their own for consumption then what will be the Base 
 Rates of those Item(s). If Rate varies at the time of actual Purchase 
 then based on this defined Base Rate and Actual Purchase Rate, Price Variation 
 will be calculated. 
 4. General Escalation Parameter 
 Engineering 
 > 
 Escalation 
 > 
 General 
 Escalation Parameter 
 At the 
 beginning of the project a parameter is finalized between the Contractor 
 and Company where Price Composition and Index Rate are finalized for Labour/Material 
 and Diesel. Based on this the General Escalation Bill will be generated. 
 5. Work Order 
 Wise Co-Ordination CFI Material Definition 
 This module is used to tag the budget head of those 
 free issue material which are provided by developer to the contractor 
 and that contractor will receive Coordination charge against that material 
 Engineering 
 > 
 Escalation > 
 Work 
 order wise CFI Material Definition 
 6. 
 Work Order Wise Approved Rate 
 Material 
 > Procurement > Purchase Order 
 7. 
 Goods Receipt Note (GRN) 
 Goods 
 Receipt Note or GRN is a document that is used to record the inward entry 
 of goods received at any establishment. The GRN primarily comprises details 
 of Quantity received, Quantity disapproved, and quantity approved. It 
 also contains information regarding name of the supplier and Purchase 
 Order Number (P.O. No.). 
 GRN 
 comes into existence when supplier supplies material at a site against 
 the purchase order (P.O.) with an intention to confirm the Stock in. GRN 
 can be processed both as Supplier wise and Party reference wise. 
 Material 
 > Receiving > Goods Receipt Note 
 8. Contractor Material Consumption (Auto 
 Issue) 
 Engineering 
 > 
 Estimation 
 > 
 Auto 
 Issue This 
 entry screen is used to keep track against each Work done entry, what 
 Materials bought by contractor are consumed (against which Price Variance 
 and General Escalation will be calculated). 
 If user wants 
 to put the Actual Consumption Quantity manually then select Manual 
 option in Resource to be shown otherwise Resource to be shown should 
 be selected as Coefficient Based (system will calculate required quantity 
 based on Coefficient defined in Resource entry). 
 In 
 Detail section, select Work done number, Activity, Original Item and 
 related substitute Item. If Coefficient Based option is selected, 
 then system will calculate the required quantity and Actual Consumed 
 quantity based on Resource defined, else required quantity has to 
 be fed manually. 
 9. Price Variance 
 Engineering 
 > 
 Escalation 
 > 
 Price 
 Variance Through 
 this entry screen user will calculate the Price Variation (if any +ve 
 or -ve) happened for the Contractor bought Items consumption due to change 
 of rate between the Base Rate and Purchase Rate. 
 10. General Escalation 
 Engineering 
 > 
 Escalation 
 > 
 General 
 Escalation Bill Time 
 to time Rate index are changed for Labour/ Material and Diesel. Due to 
 which a Price Variance Bill will be generated. 
 Open Engineering 
 > Escalation 
 > 
 General 
 Escalation menu 
 Select 
 Business Unit 
 Generate 
 Document No and put Document Date 
 Select Sub Project, 
 Contractor and proper Work Order No 
 Put 
 Party Invoice No, Party Invoice Date and Due Date 
 Put 
 Budget Code 
 Fed 
 latest value of Labour, Material and Diesel through Index Rate 
 button 
 Select 
 work done or Sub Contractor Bill(s) 
 against which General Escalation Bill will be generated from item 
 info 
 Click on Escalation 
 info, system will create escalation amount 
 11. Co-ordination 
 Charges CFI 
 In addition to the roles & responsibility defined 
 in the Annexure – A enclosed here with the contractor shall also do the

 Budget 
 Reconciliation Process: 
 We 
 already have various types of reports and based on which you can reconcile 
 the Budget vs. Utilized Amount. 
 A. Please 
 use the Budget Validation 
 Register report 
 to get the individual transaction wise cumulative utilization amount and 
 also can get Max Execution amount against a Budget Head. Please note that 
 in this report utilization and max execution amount always containing 
 provisional amount, except Budgeted Amount (Menu Path : Construction -> 
 Reports -> Budget vs Actual). 
 From 
 this report itself we can get the details against which methodology (Budget 
 Validation Logic as per Process1/Process2) system validating the Budget 
 Amount and for this purpose please refer to the Resource Wise Validation 
 Not Req. (True/False) column. If True then system validating the Process 
 No 2 Budget Validation Logic (Based on Total Budget Amount) and if False 
 then system validating the Process No 1 Budget Validation Logic (Resource 
 Wise Validation Process). 
 Each column wise 
 reconciliation details based on the other report 
 a. Budgeted Labour 
 Amount (A1): Labour 
 Amount of Project Budget Register 
 and if Amendment exists then use the Project 
 Budget Comparison report . Or you may use Project Budget Document Print 
 Format and if Amendment exists then use latest Amendment Document Print 
 Format. 
 b. Budgeted Material 
 Amount (A2): Material 
 Amount of Project Budget Register 
 and if Amendment exists then use the 
 Project Budget Comparison report . Or you may use Project Budget Document 
 Print Format and if Amendment exists then use latest Amendment Document 
 Print Format. 
 c. Budgeted Equipment 
 Amount (A3): Equipment 
 Amount of Project Budget Register 
 and if Amendment exists then use the Project 
 Budget Comparison report . Or you may use Project Budget Document Print 
 Format and if Amendment exists then use latest Amendment Document Print 
 Format. 
 d. Max Executed 
 Amount for Labour (B1): Based 
 on the Logic for Max Executed 
 Labour Amount column details and Max Executed Labour Amount will be 
 based on Resource Wise Validation Not Req. (True/False) option and PO 
 Validation Not Req. (True/False) option. 
 e. Max Executed 
 Material Amount (B2): Based 
 on the Logic for Max Executed 
 Material Amount column details and Max Executed Material Amount will 
 be based on Resource Wise Validation Not Req. (True/False) option and 
 PO Validation Not Req. (True/False) option. 
 f. Max Executed 
 Equipment Amount (B3): Based 
 on the Logic for Max Executed 
 Equipment Amount column details and Max Executed Equipment Amount 
 will be based on Resource Wise Validation Not Req. (True/False) option. 
 g. BOQ Labour Amount 
 (C1): Sum 
 of Contract Cost Amount of BOQ 
 Register . 
 h. BOQ Material 
 Amount (C2): Sum 
 of Free Issue Material Amount of BOQ 
 Register . 
 i. Work Order Labour 
 Amount (D1): Please 
 use Work Order With Amendment 
 Detail report. 
 a) 
 If Resource Wise Validation Not Required was mentioned as True then Sum 
 of Amended Amount. 
 b) 
 If Resource Wise Validation Not Required was mentioned as False then Sum 
 of Amended Amount, except Equipment Order Amended Amount. 
 j. Work Order Free 
 Issue Material Amount (D2): Sum 
 of Amount (Resource Type should be Free Issue Material) of Resource 
 Requirement Register where Option Type should be Against Work order 
 (Activity Wise - Lumpsum). 
 k. Work Order Equipment 
 Amount (D3) : 
 Please use Work Order With Amendment 
 Detail report. 
 a) 
 If Resource Wise Validation Not Req. was mentioned as False then Sum of 
 Amended Amount, except Others Order Amended Amount. 
 l. Resource Requirement 
 Against Project Budget Amount (E) : 
 Sum of Amount (Resource Type should be Free Issue Material) of Resource 
 Requirement Register where Option Type should be Against Project Budget. 
 m. Release Order 
 Amount (F) : 
 Sum Amount of Release Order Register 
 Detail report. 
 n. Purchase Order 
 Amount (G) : 
 Sum Amount (Landed Cost) of Purchase 
 Order With PO Revision Register . 
 o. Stock Adjustment 
 Amount (H) : 
 Sum Amount of Stock Adjustment 
 Register Report. 
 p. Direct Purchase 
 Bill Amount (I) : 
 Sum Debit Amount of Purchase 
 Bill Posting Detail Report where Bill Type should be Direct. 
 q. Non Store Purchase 
 Amount (Without SWO) (J) : 
 Sum Amount of Non Store Purchase 
 Register without Service Work Order. 
 r. Issued Amount 
 (- Issue Return) (K): Sum 
 Amount of Issue Register 
 - Sum Amount of Issue Return 
 Register . 
 s. Journal Voucher 
 Amount (Payroll) (L) : 
 Sum TB Amount of Budget vs Actual 
 Reconciliation Detail Report (Under Finance Module) where Transaction 
 Type should be Payroll Journal. 
 t. Journal Voucher 
 Amount (Finance) (M) : 
 Sum TB Amount of Budget vs Actual 
 Reconciliation Detail Report (Under Finance Module) where Transaction 
 Type should be Journal. 
 u. Receipt/Payment 
 Amount (Finance) (N) : 
 Sum TB Amount of Budget vs Actual 
 Reconciliation Detail Report (Under Finance Module) where Transaction 
 Type should be Receipt/Payment. 
 v. Brokerage Amount 
 (O) : Sum TB Amount of Budget 
 vs Actual Reconciliation Detail Report (Under Finance Module) where 
 Transaction Type should be Brokerage Payable. 
 B. Apart 
 from the Budget Validation Register we also have the Budget vs Actual report 
 (This report has level wise zoom in facility upto Document Detail level) 
 and which contain Company / Business Unit / Subproject / Budget Head wise 
 Budgeted and Utilization Amount in Summary and Detail manner with Date 
 filtration facility and also can define the required Amount in Figures 
 such as In Cores / In Millions / In Lakhs or Full Amount. This is a Warehouse 
 based report and process will run only at night. So if you done any transaction 
 now then the same details will appear in this report in the next morning, 
 if Approved (This report does not contain any Provisional Transactional 
 Amount). 
 Budget vs Actual Summary report is a one pager report and 
 which can be used for the Management reporting purpose and it’s also has 
 4 level of zoom in facility. 
 At 1 st Level we 
 can get individual Company wise Total Budgeted Amount, Total Committed 
 Amount, Balance to Commit Amount, Total Utilized Amount, Balance to Utilized 
 Amount (Budget vs Actual)and Completion %. 
 At 2 nd Level we 
 can get under a specific Company individual Business Unit/Project wise 
 Total Budgeted Amount, Total Committed Amount, Balance to Commit Amount, 
 Total Utilized Amount, Balance to Utilized Amount (Budget vs Actual) and 
 Completion %. 
 At 3 rd Level we 
 can get under a specific Business Unit/Project, individual Sub Project 
 wise Total Budgeted Amount, Total Committed Amount, Balance to Commit 
 Amount, Total Utilized Amount, Balance to Utilized Amount (Budget vs Actual) 
 and Completion %. 
 At 4 th Level we 
 can get under a specific Sub Project, individual Budget Group and Budget 
 Head wise Total Budgeted Amount, Total Committed Amount, Balance to Commit 
 Amount, Total Utilized Amount, Balance to Utilized Amount (Budget vs Actual) 
 and Completion %. 
 Budget vs Actual Detail report contains individual Resource 
 Wise Budgeted Amount and individual transaction wise Committed and Utilized 
 Amount and it’s also has level wise zoom in facility like Sub Project 
 Wise, Budget Head Wise and Sub Project Budget Head Wise etc. From this 
 report itself we can zoom upto Document Detail level. For getting the 
 Document Detail against a Budget Head please zoom in through below mention 
 columns such as 
 Under

 Order Amount (Order Value - Taxes (ITC)),

 Under

 a) RA 
 Bill Amount (Bill Amount - Taxes (ITC)),

 c) Other

 d) Other 
 Expenses Amount With Order (Bill Amount - Taxes (ITC)), 
 Under 
 Material Consumption Section : 
 a) Material 
 Issued Amount 
 Each column wise 
 reconciliation details based on the other report 
 a. Budgeted Labour 
 Amount (A1) : 
 Labour Amount of Project Budget 
 Register and if Amendment exists then use the Project

 Format. 
 b. Budgeted Material 
 Amount (A2): Material 
 Amount of Project Budget Register 
 and if Amendment exists then use the 
 Project Budget Comparison report . Or you may use Project Budget Document 
 Print Format and if Amendment exists then use latest Amendment Document

 c. Work Order Amount 
 (Order Value - Taxes (ITC)) (B) : Sum 
 Amended Amount (Report Option should be Approved) of Work

 Amount + Work Order Taxes 
 Amount (Non ITC). 
 d. Free Material 
 Amount (B3) : Sum 
 of Amount (Resource Type should be Free Issue Material) of Resource 
 Requirement Register where Option Type should be Against Work order 
 (Activity Wise - Lumpsum). 
 e. Release Order 
 Amount (Order Value - Taxes (ITC)) (C) : 
 Sum Amount of Release Order Register 
 Detail report + Release Order 
 Taxes Amount (Non ITC). 
 f. Purchase Order 
 Amount (Order Value - Taxes (ITC Amount)) (D) : Sum 
 Amount of Purchase Order With 
 PO Revision Register + Purchase 
 Order Taxes (Non ITC). 
 g. Opening Budgeted 
 Amount for Labour (E1) : Contract Cost Opening Executed Amount 
 of Project Budget Entry . 
 h. Opening Budgeted 
 Amount for Material (E2) : Free Issue Material Opening Executed 
 Amount of Project Budget 
 Entry . 
 i. Other Expenses 
 Amount Without Order (Bill Amount - Taxes (ITC)) (F) : Sum Debit Amount of Purchase 
 Bill Posting Detail Report where Bill Type should be Direct + Sum 
 Amount of Non Store Purchase 
 Register without order + Sum TB Amount of Budget vs Actual Reconciliation 
 Detail Report where Transaction Type should be Payroll Journal + Sum 
 TB Amount of Budget 
 vs Actual Reconciliation Detail Report where 
 Transaction Type should be Journal + Sum TB Amount of Budget vs Actual Reconciliation 
 Detail Report where Transaction Type should be Receipt/Payment + Sum 
 TB Amount of Budget vs Actual 
 Reconciliation Detail Report where 
 Transaction Type should be Brokerage Payable + Other 
 Expenses Taxes Without Order (Non ITC Amount) . Only Expense related 
 voucher details will appear in this column. 
 j. RA Bill Amount 
 (Bill Amount - Taxes (ITC)) (I) : Sum Amount of Contractor 
 RA Bill Register Detail Report (Excluding Opening Bill) + RA 
 Bill Taxes (Non ITC Amount). 
 k. Purchase Bill 
 Amount (Bill Amount - Taxes (ITC)) (J) : Sum Debit - Credit Amount of Purchase Bill Posting Detail 
 Report where Bill Type should be Against GRN + Purchase 
 Bill Taxes (Non ITC Amount). 
 l. Other Expenses

 Bill Posting Detail Report where Bill Type should be Direct + Sum 
 Amount of Non Store Purchase 
 Register without Order + Sum TB Amount of Budget vs Actual Reconciliation 
 Detail Report where Transaction Type should be Payroll Journal + Sum 
 TB Amount of Budget 
 vs Actual Reconciliation Detail Report where 
 Transaction Type should be Journal + Sum TB Amount of Budget vs Actual Reconciliation 
 Detail Report where Transaction Type should be Receipt/Payment + Sum 
 TB Amount of Budget vs Actual 
 Reconciliation Detail Report where 
 Transaction Type should be Brokerage Payable + Other

 of Issue Return Register

 Mobile Configuration 
 Mobile configuration is required for each mobile app (both IOS and android) to enable push notifications. For details about Enterprise Name, server public IP and app credentials, please refer to the detailed help on Mobile Configuration . 
 Download Farvision Approval App from 
 1. Apple Apps Store (For IOS) 
 2. Android Store (For Android) 
 Please type FV Approval on Google Play Store/Apple Apps Store to find and download the mobile application or download from the following URLs 
 Download Links 
 For IOS 
 https://apps.apple.com/in/app/farvisionapprovalr2/id1435066074 
 For Android 
 https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gamut.farvisionapprovalr2&hl=en_IN&gl=US 
 Cloud SetUp 
 Step1: Install and open FV Approval App. Press 'Configure Your App' to setup your account. 
 Step2: Press ‘Cloud SetUp’ if your Farvision application runs on Farvision Cloud server. Please contact your administrator to know your cloud server name. Choose your cloud server from “Cloud SetUp” option.

 OR 
 Set Up

 Step2 : Enter your Enterprise name and on premises server URL/IP. HTTPS is required to be checked if your server is SSL certified and you have entered domain name. If you have entered IP Address as server url then SSL is not required hence left this unchecked.

title: Dashboard
text:
Dashboard 
 Mobile App > Task Management App" />
 Dashboard 
 Login to the Mobile App 
 Open 
 the Task Management Mobile Application and log in using your corporate 
 credentials via SSO/IDP. SSO (Single Sign-On )allows 
 a user to log in once using their company credentials and then 
 access multiple apps (like the Task Management App, Farvision modules, 
 etc.) without entering the password again . An IDP (Identity 
 Provider) is the system that verifies the user’s identity when 
 they log in. 
 After 
 successful login, the user lands on the Dashboard by default. 
 2. Understand 
 the Dashboard Overview 
The Dashboard shows a doughnut chart that summarizes 
 all tasks into four key categories – Total, Pending, 
 Overdue, and Completed . This helps the user quickly understand their 
 overall workload and task status at a glance. 
 1. Pending Tasks 
 Pending tasks are all tasks that have been 
 created but are not yet marked as Completed . 
This includes tasks that are within their allowed time window (i.e., not 
 overdue). 
In practical terms, the Pending count shows how 
 much work is still open and needs to be completed by the user or their 
 team . 
Users typically monitor this section daily to plan their work and prioritize 
 items that are approaching their deadlines. 
 2. 
 Overdue Tasks 
 Overdue tasks are those where the End Date 
 and End Time have already passed , but the task has not 
 been updated to Completed . 
The system automatically calculates overdue status, updating it within 
 about a minute after the end time is crossed. 
This category is critical because it highlights tasks that have breached 
 their timeline and require immediate attention or escalation. 
Overdue tasks impact the user’s and team’s performance metrics and often 
 trigger follow-up actions. 
 3. 
 Completed Tasks 
 Completed tasks are those where the Assignee has 
 marked the task as Completed , and the system has successfully 
 recorded the status update. 
This section allows users to review their completed workload and confirm 
 that all necessary tasks have been properly closed. 
Completion updates reflect across all views — Dashboard, Task Board, and 
 BU-wise view — ensuring accurate progress reporting. 
 4. 
 Total Tasks 
 Total is the sum of Pending + Overdue + 
 Completed tasks under the selected category (General or Reference) 
 and applied filters (BU, Contractor). 
It serves as a high-level indicator of the overall task volume within the 
 user’s scope. 
 3. 
 Switch Between General and Reference Tasks 
At the top of the Dashboard, the user can toggle between General 
 and Reference tabs. 
 General 
 shows 
 standalone tasks not linked to any work order. 
 Reference 
 shows 
 tasks that are tied to a Business Unit, Contractor, Work Order, 
 Activity, and Milestone. 
 The doughnut chart and counts refresh immediately based on the 
 selected tab. 
 4. 
 Use Filters on 
 the Dashboard 
The Dashboard supports filters such as Business Unit (for both General 
 and Reference tasks) and Contractor (for Reference tasks). When 
 the user applies filters, all counts and percentages in the doughnut chart 
 and list views are recalculated according to the selected filter values. 
 5.Use 
 “Today’s Task” Quick Action 
The Today’s Task button shows all tasks where the start date 
 or end date equals the current device date . This allows users to quickly 
 focus on what needs to be worked on or completed today , without 
 manually filtering dates. 
 6.Use 
 “+ New Task” Quick Action 
The + New Task button is the primary entry point for creating new 
 tasks. From here, users can choose whether they want to create a General 
 Task or a Reference Task , and then proceed with the appropriate 
 form. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited
